newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatilities flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatilities flat to lower.

text.p: Flat U.S. stock indexes led to flat index options trading Friday, dealers said.
Most indexes ended the day with modest losses after having spent time in both positive and negative territory.
The Dow industrials .DJI eased about 3-1/2 points to 8,113, the S&P 500 .SPX fell about 1-1/2 to 939 and the S&P 100 .OEX lost nearly one to 918.
All three reached record intraday highs.
Traders said activity was sluggish, with volatilities generally flat to down. Softness was attributed mainly to time decay ahead of the weekend.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), the volatility index, which is calculated off certain OEX contracts, rose 0.01 to 23.49.
In the OEX, put volume outpaced call volume by 26,346 to 22,273. Activity was led by the August 950 calls, which had volume of 3,030 contracts.
SPX puts traded 59,065 contracts compared with 17,884 calls. The heaviest action was in the August 900 puts, which traded more than 12,800 contracts.
Other active SPX puts included the August 920s, the December 900s and the September 900s.
One options dealer in Chicago said order flow continued to focus on individual equity options rather than index options and in calls rather than puts.
"We have seen on this desk a lot more call buying," he said. "Generally in these kind of (market) moves, you get a lot of people speculating on puts in the OEX.
"I have not," he said, adding that the heavy interest in equity calls is one suggestion the market is "a bit on the frothy side."
